# Demo B popup loads its example styling

## Context and problem

The operator observed an unstyled Workbench popup during the headed keyboard regression run for #20492. A focused browser probe confirmed the pane remains plain after mount and network idle: the parent has the example palette and Demo A/B sheets; the popup has only basic Neo sheets. Its counter falls from 34px to 16px and its flex card becomes a block. No CSS request fails—the relevant files are never requested.

## Architectural reality and fix

`examples/dashboard/crossWindow/Viewport.mjs` deliberately creates an empty render target for `?popout=`; it does not instantiate `DemoBWorkspace`. The latter currently declares the example palette and Demo A skin, and its own stylesheet contains the CounterPane and popout-host rules. `CounterPane` has no own stylesheet dependency. `App#insertThemeFiles` loads dependencies per window, so the main window's sheets are not inherited by the popup.

Declare the existing shared example palette and Demo A/B styling on the viewport that exists in both boot modes. Keep the popup a pure render target; no extra workspace, pane recreation, global CSS injection or Engine theme-loader change. The shared example viewport/workspace rules must explicitly specialize the Engine classes so later-loaded base CSS cannot replace the example background; CI's existing dark/light palette assertions exposed that cascade dependency.

Prescription checked: `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/Viewport.mjs` — owns the two render-target modes and their shared visual shell. Prior #15923 addressed a distinct Workstation token-bridge scope defect; it does not fix this example's absent stylesheet dependencies.

| Traveling Workbench pane | CounterPane + existing keyboard detach journey | Same live pane renders as the styled card after reparenting | Counter continuity and ordinary popup lifecycle preserved | Existing class docs | Headed screenshot and existing native journey |
| Regression check | DemoBKeyboardDetachNL first journey | Assert visible pane styling, not only popup/announcement existence | Fails on old dependency declaration; no test-injected styles | Test assertion context | Red-before-fix / green-after-fix browser check |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A real Workbench popup loads its example palette and styling through declared dependencies, with no test CSS injection or failing CSS requests.
- [ ] Its card display, counter typography and palette colors match the parent before detach; headed screenshot verifies the intended appearance.
- [ ] The existing keyboard popup journey retains worker instance continuity and truthfully announces focus; its new style assertions fail on the previous viewport and pass after the fix.

## Out of scope

Keyboard decomposition (#20492), command semantics, window acquisition, general theme-loader redesign, and Workstation's separate styling contract.

Decision Record impact: none; declared theme dependencies restore existing visual intent.
